recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Women, the new sharks shaping the future of startup investment in Australia | The Business
recentItems.description:
They're called venture capitalists or sharks.
Australia's venture capital industry has long been dominated by men but as more women jump in, the kind of startups getting up is starting to change.
 Investors are navigating a complex world of high risk and legislative change. 
Major VC firm, Main Sequence was started by the CSIRO.
It's one of Australia's biggest deep-tech investors with more than $1 billion under management. 
The investment team was once all-male but now it's 50 per cent women. 
Last year, a report found startups received more than 5 billion dollars in funding, but just 2 per cent went to teams led entirely by women.
A growing number of venture capital firms are now tracking and sharing gender diversity data about their teams and deals, and there's a push among advocates for national standards.

However, the industry is worried the government's tax changes will push investors away from taking big risks on these types of companies to invest in established firms already offering returns. 

Australian Investment Council chief executive, Navleen Prasad says they are concerned about a "capital crunch or capital squeeze", particularly for early stage startups and scale up businesses in Australia.

recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: UN votes to adopt a new world map | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The United Nations has voted to adopt a new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, replacing the Mercator projection maps. 

The old maps feature several inaccuracies, such as a larger North America, Europe and Greenland against a smaller Africa, Latin America and Oceania. 

Grace McKinnon for ABC News Loop.

recentItems.title: German far-right party AfD wins state election | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The Alternative for Germany party has won more than 44 per cent of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, by far the most of any party.
The result means a far-right party is on the cusp of forming government at the state level in Germany for the first time since World War II.
